q: A Collector treats a State Finance Commission recommendation as binding and refuses to release funds otherwise. Which statement is correct?
options: The recommendation is advisory; the State decides and records reasons for its decision
The recommendation is binding once laid before the State legislature
The recommendation is binding on the executive but not on the legislature
The recommendation is advisory but becomes binding after one year
expl: Finance Commission recommendations are advisory at both Union and State level.
why: The second option ties bindingness to the act of laying, which is a procedural step and not a source of obligation.
trapnote: Laying a report before a House does not convert advice into obligation.

q: A liquor outlet is licensed in a Scheduled Area without reference to the village assembly. Which statement is correct?
options: The municipal licence is conclusive, the assembly having only advisory functions
The assembly has no power over intoxicants, its powers being confined to land
The assembly's power arises only where the outlet is within panchayat limits
The assembly may regulate or prohibit intoxicants, so the licence is open to challenge
expl: Regulation or prohibition of intoxicants is among the powers conferred on the assembly.
why: The third option narrows the powers to land alone, which is the most common underestimate of the scheme.
trapnote: The powers extend well beyond land: intoxicants, minor minerals, produce and money lending.

q: It is argued that excluding certain areas from the uniform local government structure is discriminatory. Which statement is correct?
options: The exclusion is discriminatory and has been read down by the courts
The exclusion is valid because the Constitution cannot be challenged for inequality
The exclusion rests on a real difference connected to protecting local self-governance
The exclusion is valid only where the State legislature has approved it
expl: The classification is founded on an intelligible difference bearing a nexus to a protective object.
why: The third option states a proposition about constitutional provisions that is too broad to be accurate.
trapnote: The exclusion is a classification with a protective object, and it satisfies the usual test.

q: Elections in four mandals are deferred by the State Election Commission because of floods, and bias is alleged. Which statement is correct?
options: The Commission has no power to defer, the five-year term being mandatory
The Commission has independent power to defer, and the decision stands absent mala fides
The deferment requires the prior approval of the State government
The deferment is valid only if the High Court confirms it within thirty days
expl: Superintendence of local elections vests in the Commission and its decisions are reviewable only on limited grounds.
why: The second option converts a term limit into a bar on any deferment, which would make floods legally irrelevant.
trapnote: Independent electoral authorities have operational discretion, reviewable on limited grounds.

q: Consider: 1-The rural Part applies to Scheduled Areas of its own force. 2-Parliament may extend it to those areas with modifications. 3-Parliament did so in 1996. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: It does not apply of its own force; the power to extend was exercised in 1996.
why: The exclusion and the extension are two halves of one arrangement, and the first statement denies the exclusion.
trapnote: Excluded by one provision, restored by a later law. That is the whole architecture.

q: A new district is created and a Zilla Parishad is constituted for it. Which statement is correct about audit of its funds?
options: Audit is conducted by the State Election Commission as part of its supervision
Audit is conducted by the district collector and reported to the State government
Audit is conducted by the State Finance Commission in its five-yearly review
Audit follows the constitutional audit machinery and the State legislature's scrutiny
expl: Audit rests with the constitutional auditor and scrutiny with the legislature.
why: The fourth option confuses a body that reviews the financial position with a body that audits accounts.
trapnote: Reviewing a financial position and auditing accounts are different functions and different bodies.

q: Consider the village assembly and the village panchayat: 1-The assembly consists of all registered voters. 2-The panchayat is the elected body. 3-In a Scheduled Area the panchayat has primacy over the assembly. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: In a Scheduled Area primacy rests with the assembly, not the elected body.
why: The inversion of the ordinary relationship between the two bodies is the defining feature of the special scheme.
trapnote: Ordinary areas: the elected body governs. Scheduled Areas: the assembly has primacy.

q: A State provides one-half reservation for women in local bodies. Which statement is correct?
options: Impermissible: the Constitution prescribes one-third and a State may not vary it
Permissible: the Constitution prescribes a floor and a State may exceed it
Permissible only with the prior approval of the President of India
Impermissible: reservation above one-half of total seats is void in all cases
expl: The constitutional provision is a minimum, not a ceiling.
why: The fourth option imports the ceiling doctrine from public employment, where it applies to a different subject.
trapnote: A floor invites exceeding; a ceiling forbids it. Identify which one the provision creates.

q: Consider: 1-A panchayat may levy taxes if authorised by State law. 2-A panchayat may levy taxes of its own force under the Constitution. 3-Grants-in-aid may be made from the Consolidated Fund of the State. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: Tax only if authorised by State law; no own-force power; grants-in-aid from the State fund valid.
why: The pattern is the same as with subjects: the Constitution enables and the State legislature confers.
trapnote: Local bodies derive powers from State law. The Constitution enables rather than confers.

q: Polls are delayed, funds are withheld and no district plan is prepared. Which combination identifies the correct institutional responses?
options: The election commission for all three, its supervision extending to funds and plans
The State government for polls and funds, the planning committee for plans alone
The finance commission for polls and funds, the election commission for plans
Election commission for polls, finance commission for devolution, planning committee for plans
expl: Three functions rest with three different bodies.
why: The instinct to consolidate all three under one authority is what the item is designed to defeat.
trapnote: Three problems, three bodies. The separation of these functions is deliberate.
